summary.text: Shontel Brown is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in Ohio's 11th Congressional District, which she has represented since winning a 2021 special election. A lifelong Clevelander and former marketing professional and small-business owner, she served on the Warrensville Heights city council and the Cuyahoga County Council and chaired the Cuyahoga County Democratic Party. In Congress she is vice ranking member of the House Agriculture Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1975; her official biography describes her as a lifelong Clevelander and says she lives in Warrensville Heights.
Earned an associate degree in business management from Cuyahoga Community College and a bachelor's degree in organizational management from Wilberforce University.

Owned Diversified Digital Solutions and worked as director of sales for Hotcards.com, a senior account manager with Radio One, and a marketing support representative with Telco Communications Group before her political career.

Entered public service in 2012 as a Warrensville Heights city council member, according to her official biography. In 2014 she was elected to the Cuyahoga County Council to represent the 9th district, and she served on it until 2021.
Elected chair of the Cuyahoga County Democratic Party in 2017, becoming the first woman and first African American to hold the post.

Won the August 2021 Democratic primary and the November 2, 2021 special general election to succeed Marcia Fudge, who resigned to become Secretary of Housing and Urban Development; she was sworn in on November 4, 2021. She defeated former state Sen. Nina Turner in the 2022 Democratic primary.

In the 119th Congress serves on the House Agriculture Committee as vice ranking member, on the Oversight Committee (ranking member of its Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation Subcommittee) and on the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, according to her official biography.

Is a member of the Congressional Black Caucus, the New Democrat Coalition and the Congressional Progressive Caucus, among other caucuses; her official biography says she has authored bills on the racial health gap and anti-discrimination law.
